subject: Quant
topic: Time, speed and distance II — mixed tiers
description: Average speed, relative speed, trains, boats

questions.stem: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 120 / 2 = 60 km/h. A common trap is 120 (total distance, not speed) or 40 (from wrong division). Note — average speed over a trip is not always the arithmetic mean of individual-leg speeds; it is total distance divided by total time.

questions.stem: A man covers a distance at 40 km/h and returns along the same route at 60 km/h. His average speed for the entire journey is:
questions.explanation: For equal distances at different speeds, average speed = harmonic mean = 2ab/(a+b) = 2 × 40 × 60 / (40+60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h. The arithmetic mean 50 is a classic trap. Proof — let distance each way = 120 km; time at 40 km/h = 3 h, time at 60 km/h = 2 h; total 240 km in 5 h → 48 km/h.

questions.stem: A train 150 m long travelling at 72 km/h takes how many seconds to cross a stationary pole?
questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 72 × (5/18) m/s = 20 m/s. Time to cross a pole = length of train / speed = 150 / 20 = 7.5 s. Remember — to cross a pole, only the length of the train matters; to cross a bridge, the length of the train + length of the bridge.

questions.stem: Two trains of length 120 m and 180 m are moving in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. The time they take to completely cross each other is:
questions.explanation: For opposite directions, relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s. Total distance to clear = 120 + 180 = 300 m. Time = 300/25 = 12 s. If the trains were running in the same direction, the relative speed would be 54 − 36 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s, giving time = 300/5 = 60 s.

questions.stem: A boat rows 24 km downstream in 2 hours and 24 km upstream in 3 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 24/2 = 12 km/h = b + s (boat + stream). Upstream speed = 24/3 = 8 km/h = b − s. Adding: 2b = 20 → b = 10 km/h. Subtracting: 2s = 4 → s = 2 km/h. Always — boat speed = (down + up)/2; stream speed = (down − up)/2.

questions.stem: A person walks at 5 km/h, 4 hours a day. How far will he walk in 3 days?
questions.explanation: Daily distance = speed × time per day = 5 × 4 = 20 km. Over 3 days → 20 × 3 = 60 km. 20 is one day's distance (trap); 12 comes from multiplying 4 and 3 only (ignoring speed); 15 is 5 × 3 (ignoring daily hours).

questions.stem: A train running at 60 km/h crosses a 180-m-long bridge in 21 seconds. The length of the train is:
questions.explanation: Speed = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s. Total distance covered in 21 s = 50/3 × 21 = 350 m. Train length = 350 − 180 (bridge length) = 170 m. To cross a bridge, total distance = length of train + length of bridge.
